newsitem.title: USA: S&P says looks favorably on James River merger.
newsitem.headline: S&P says looks favorably on James River merger.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said it will look very favorably on the combined business position of James River Corp and Fort Howard Corp in its review of the merger, said Cindy Werneth, an associate director at S&P.

"The two companies have said they are complementary in terms of business focus and geography," Werneth said. "James River's strengths are in marketing and product development whereas Fort Howard's are on the operating and manufacturing side. So we see them as a nice fit for each other."
Werneth would not comment on the fate of the agency's outstanding positive outlook for James River ratings.

The assumption of $2.4 billion in Fort Howard debt will undoubtedly make for a more highly leveraged James River, she said, but that will be pitted against strong cash flows. The ability of the new entity to service that debt will be more heavily weighted in the review, she said.
"Despite the high debt I think they are still going to have fairly healty cash flows, and we'll weigh that probably more than just the way the balance sheet looks per se," Werneth said.
S&P currently rates James River's senior unsecured debt BBB-minus with a positive outlook. Moody's Investors Service rates the debt Baa3.
Werneth said the agency is working on a full comment. Moody's did not return a phone call.
Analysts and company executives both noted that the rating agencies were not consulted on the planned merger.

James River and Fort Howard said on Monday they signed a definitive merger agreement to create a $7 billion paper and tissue products company to be called Fort James Corp. It is a stock for stock transaction in a deal valued at $5.8 billion, including the assumption of debt.
